payload.summary: Fix final_price() in pricing.py so the tax_rate argument takes effect by applying tax on top of the discounted price. Expected: final_price(100, 0.2, 0.1) == 88.0 (discounted 80.0 * 1.1).

tasks.title: Apply tax_rate in final_price()
tasks.description: In pricing.py, modify final_price(price, discount, tax_rate) so it returns the discounted price multiplied by (1 + tax_rate), e.g. return apply_discount(price, discount) * (1 + tax_rate). Keep the existing apply_discount validation behavior. Do not change other files.

tasks.title: Run tests to verify final_price tax behavior
tasks.description: Run the test suite (pytest tests/test_shop.py) and confirm test_final_price, test_order_total, test_order_coupon, and test_summarize all pass after the pricing.py fix.

findings: pricing.py:11-12 defines final_price(price, discount, tax_rate) but the body only returns apply_discount(price, discount), so tax_rate is ignored. The fix is to multiply the discounted price by (1 + tax_rate).
apply_discount(price, discount) validates discount in [0, 1) and returns price * (1 - discount); this behavior must be preserved.
order.py:8 and report.py:6 both call final_price(item['price'], discount, tax_rate) and rely on the tax_rate taking effect.

Tests in tests/test_shop.py already encode expected tax behavior: final_price(100, 0.2, 0.1) == 88.0; order_total for two 100/50 items with 0.2 discount and 0.1 tax == 132.0; order_coupon == 78.0; summarize totals/average/max all assume tax applied.

changes: final_price() now applies tax_rate by returning apply_discount(price, discount) * (1 + tax_rate)

payload.summary: Ran python3 -m pytest tests/test_shop.py -q: 7 passed. Lint/syntax check via py_compile passed. pricing.py final_price now returns apply_discount(price, discount) * (1 + tax_rate), so tax_rate takes effect.

suggestions: The fix is minimal and correct: final_price() now returns apply_discount(price, discount) * (1 + tax_rate), so the tax_rate argument takes effect on top of the discounted price.
Existing apply_discount() validation is preserved because final_price() delegates to it unchanged.
Downstream callers (order.py, report.py) rely only on final_price() and remain consistent with the new behavior; test_report confirms all 7 tests pass.
Optional future hardening: consider using Decimal for monetary math to avoid floating-point rounding, though this is out of scope for this feature.
